label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
@Kavya, I’m writing because people are tagging me in your post, and I don’t want silence to leave a few things standing as fact. But I don’t want this to become a public fight between us either.

We were in Foundry91 cohort 4 together, with demo day in March 2026. You’re building SitterNest, I’m building DabbaDost. Before that demo day, you sat with me till 1am in the Koramangala office fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. I haven’t forgotten that, or how much you’ve helped me.

First, the part I got wrong: I knew from day one where both candidates worked. I should have called you before making the offers, not told you once the second offer was accepted. That was poor judgment on my part. I’m sorry.

I do need to correct three things, without naming either person. They didn’t ask to be part of a public discussion, and I won’t put their names here.

We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. The first candidate applied himself on 19 September. The second came through his referral two weeks later. Nobody from our side DMed either of them.

Both offers were 22% above their current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November. I’m putting the number here because I don’t want 40% to keep getting repeated as fact.

On ESOPs: we do have a pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January. We did not promise ESOPs from a pool that doesn’t exist.

I WhatsApped you after the second offer was accepted. That message should have been a call much earlier. Getting the hiring facts straight doesn’t let me off the hook for how I handled this with you.

There are 11 startups in our batch, hiring from the same small pool around HSR and Koramangala. This will come up again. I’d suggest one simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer.

Not to ask permission, or take away anyone’s choice about where they work. Just so a founder hears it directly from a peer, rather than after the decision is made.

Kavya, I respect you and value our friendship. I can own my mistake without agreeing with every claim in the post. Coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re okay with it. I’d much rather talk to you than keep talking about this online.
